bullets.title: Semis under pressure: DeepSeek chip dev, China AI budget shift weigh on NVDA/MU/AMD
bullets.body: Pre-market semis sold off sharply — WDC -7.2%, SNDK -5.7%, MU -5.1%, AMD -4.4%, NVDA -1.6% — on Reuters report of DeepSeek developing its own inference chip and Chinese firms raising domestic AI accelerator budget share from 30% to 46%. MS notes Samsung -9% despite 19x y/y profit growth, arguing memory is approaching 'peak rate of change'; Klein counters that Q3 DRAM ASPs are tracking +20-30% QoQ and server CPU demand is structurally bullish for AMD/INTC.

bullets.title: AAPL PT raised to $345 at JPM; AVGO-AAPL ASIC deal expands through 2031
bullets.body: JPM raises AAPL PT to $345 (32x CY28E EPS) on price elasticity resilience — FY27E EPS unchanged at $9.85 despite ~20% avg price hikes on iPads/Macs. AVGO-AAPL AI/datacenter partnership expanded through 2031 to include CPU and eventual XPU, potentially pushing AVGO Apple ASIC revenue to 'multi-billions annually.' AAPL App Store grew ~2% in June per UBS.

bullets.title: META: MS bullish on 'time to power' read-through; states seek $1.4T in penalties
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues META's cloud expansion confirms compute power as the critical AI bottleneck, with META capex growing from $145B (2026) to $205B (2028) and 3.5 GW of capacity added; every 250 MW leased adds ~$3 (8%) to 2028 EPS. Separately, four US states (CO, CA, KY, NJ) are seeking ~$1.4T in penalties over allegedly addictive Facebook/Instagram design, and SCOTUS declined to block Texas age-verification law.

bullets.title: GOOGL/AMZN/MSFT: Internet sector +6% YTD; Jefferies flags AI capex return risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports internet names up 6% YTD vs SPX +2%; GOOGL +7% at 25x 2026E EPS (down 20% vs TTM avg), META +6% at 23x, AMZN +4% at 25x. Jefferies warns of rising risk that investors question returns on debt-financed AI capex, with hyperscaler share prices cited as the key confidence indicator; US 10Y >4.5% flagged as equity warning signal.

bullets.title: APP: Citi defends eCommerce thesis; Hong Kong store decline is dropshipper churn, not demand
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on APP at $710 PT (32x 2027E FCF); Store Leads data showing flat AppLovin Ads growth reflects ~400 related Hong Kong dropshipping storefronts that installed then uninstalled the product, not genuine customer churn. Separately, MS notes APP +10% YTD in the internet sector recap.

bullets.title: WULF/BE/CEG/SEI: MS bullish on 'time to power' stocks despite last week's selloff
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Stephen Byrd argues 'powered shells' are commanding $10-12/watt economics with 15-19% unlevered FCF yields — 15x higher value creation than renewable PPAs — and that the group was severely oversold last week (WULF -19%, SEI -15%, VST -10%). Citi also remains a buyer of WULF following its data lease and JV sale announcements, with shares up ~10%.

bullets.title: EFX: Multiple firms bullish on $750M Círculo de Crédito acquisition
bullets.body: UBS (Buy, $220 PT), Mizuho (Outperform, $210 PT), and MS (Overweight) all positive on EFX's $750M acquisition of Círculo de Crédito, Mexico's #2 credit bureau with ~33% market share, 31% revenue growth, and 46% EBITDA margins. Deal valued at 11.7x FY26E EBITDA (9.4x with synergies), expected EPS-accretive in year one, closes 4Q26; Mexico credit bureau market growing 15% CAGR to ~$600M by 2029.

bullets.title: DOCN: KeyBanc raises PT to $200 after RPO triples to $800M+ on nine-figure wins
bullets.body: DigitalOcean pre-announced 2Q26 RPO jumping to $800M+ (up ~230% from $243M in 1Q26), driven by nine-figure customer wins for inference/cloud with average deal terms of 3.5+ years vs 1.6 years prior. Revenue growth now expected ~29% in 2Q with profitability guidance met or exceeded; company secured 20 MW of new capacity for end-2027/2028 and sees 30+ MW additional feasible.

bullets.title: FSLR upgraded to Buy at Deutsche Bank; PT raised to $272
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank upgrades FSLR from Hold to Buy, raising PT to $272 from $245, citing a stronger second half outlook and S232 policy clarifications. Shares up ~3.1% pre-market.

bullets.title: CART: Extreme options activity — 730% volume spike, P/C ratio 0.01
bullets.body: Instacart saw options volume surge to 22,464 contracts vs a 3,079 30-day average (+730%), with a P/C ratio of 0.01 indicating overwhelmingly call-heavy positioning. No fundamental catalyst was cited in the note.

bullets.title: RDDT/SNAP: Strong YTD performance; internet sector note flags AI commerce risk
bullets.body: RDDT +17% and SNAP +10% YTD per MS internet sector recap. Roth flagging AI commerce shift risk for both as product discovery migrates toward AI assistants, with attribution measurement and platform visibility in ChatGPT/Gemini as key open questions.

bullets.title: HUBS: Oppenheimer hosting expert call today on Q2 trends, AI pricing, Revenue Hub
bullets.body: Oppenheimer arranged a 1pm ET HubSpot partner expert call covering 2Q customer/conversion trends, Revenue Hub early feedback, AI credit pricing/consumption behavior, and competitive dynamics vs CRM.

bullets.title: AVGO: Wolfe hosting management wrap-up webcast tomorrow (7/8 at 11am ET)
bullets.body: Wolfe Research hosting AVGO post-earnings management wrap-up call on July 8 at 11am ET. No substantive views disclosed in the invite itself.

bullets.title: VRT/ENPH: OPCO flags data center 800VDC architecture shift as catalyst
bullets.body: OPCO sales desk notes data centers migrating to 800VDC architectures, creating solid-state transformer and BESS opportunities. ENPH and other power electronics firms positioned for the transition; VRT developing rack-scale solutions for BESS.

bullets.title: CMCSA/T/VZ: MS cuts telco/cable PTs on SpaceX Starlink threat
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley cuts telco/cable price targets in its SpaceX initiation: T $30→$25, CMCSA $33→$30, VZ unchanged at $50; TMUS cut to $230 from $260 but remains Top Pick for fastest growth/least legacy. Cable broadband subs modeled to decline ~3-4% CAGR through 2030 as Satellite gains >30% CAGR.

bullets.title: CLS: Down 5.5% in Canadian trading amid broad semi/AI infra de-grossing
bullets.body: Celestica trading down 5.5% to C$470.51 in mid-morning Canadian trading, consistent with the broader AI infrastructure de-risking wave hitting the sector.

bullets.title: SHOP: Up 2.2% in Canadian trading; AI commerce webinar flags platform risk
bullets.body: Shopify trading up 2.2% to C$174.38 in Canadian mid-morning session. Roth AI commerce expert call today flags product discovery shift toward AI assistants as a potential headwind/tailwind for SHOP's merchant base.

bullets.title: WSM: KeyBanc raises PT to $250; favors LOW, WSM on hardlines share gain
bullets.body: KeyBanc raises WSM PT to $250 from $230, citing K-shaped consumer spending dynamics and significant upside in home-related coverage from unsustainable lows. Firm also sees share gain opportunities for LOW among hardlines/broadlines names.

bullets.title: TTWO: Benchmark maintains Buy/$300 PT; GTA 6 online ecosystem is the long-term monetization story
bullets.body: Benchmark keeps Buy/$300 PT on TTWO, viewing GTA 6 as the company's biggest launch ever but emphasizing that the real upside is the extended online ecosystem, premium DLC, creator integration, and AI enhancements over multi-year engagement cycle.

bullets.title: Momentum factor -23% in 10 days; MS QDS flags semi/AI leverage as tail risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley QDS reports the MSZZMOMO momentum factor is down 23% from its June 23 peak in just 10 business days (vs. historical median ~30), driven equally by long underperformance (-12%) and short outperformance (+13%). Levered ETFs are short gamma in Semis (-$1.7B/1% SOX), NDX (-$2.8B/1%), and AI single names (-$1.3B/1%); SK Hynix ADR supply this week adds additional pressure. Feb 2021 comparable saw another -18% after a similar pattern.
